questions.question: Which word is a noun in this sentence: 'The dog chased the ball quickly.'?
questions.explanation: A noun names a person, place, thing, or idea. Dog is a thing.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: nouns name things - dog is a noun!

questions.question: Which word is a verb in this sentence: 'Sara runs every morning.'?
questions.explanation: A verb shows action. Runs is the action.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: verbs show action - runs is the action!

questions.question: Which word is an adjective in this sentence: 'The tall tree swayed in the wind.'?
questions.explanation: An adjective describes a noun. Tall describes the tree.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: adjectives describe nouns - tall describes the tree!

questions.question: Which word is an adverb in this sentence: 'He spoke quietly to his friend.'?
questions.explanation: An adverb describes a verb. Quietly tells how he spoke.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: adverbs tell how - quietly tells how he spoke!

questions.question: Which word is a pronoun in this sentence: 'She gave him the book.'?
questions.explanation: A pronoun takes the place of a noun. She stands for a girl or woman.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: pronouns stand in for nouns - she does the job!

questions.question: Which of these is a proper noun?
questions.explanation: A proper noun names a specific place or person and starts with a capital letter.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: proper nouns are specific names - Phoenix!

questions.question: Which of these is a common noun?
questions.explanation: A common noun names a general person, place, or thing.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: common nouns are general - teacher!

questions.question: Which word is a preposition in this sentence: 'The cat hid under the bed.'?
questions.explanation: A preposition shows where something is. Under shows where the cat hid.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: prepositions show where - under the bed!

questions.question: Which word is a conjunction in this sentence: 'I wanted to play, but it was raining.'?
questions.explanation: A conjunction joins words or sentences. But joins the two ideas.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: conjunctions join ideas - but links them!

questions.question: Which word is an interjection in this sentence: 'Wow! That was amazing.'?
questions.explanation: An interjection shows strong feeling, like Wow or Ouch.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: wow shows big feeling - that is an interjection!

questions.question: What is the subject of this sentence: 'The birds sang in the morning.'?
questions.explanation: The subject is who or what the sentence is about.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the subject is who the sentence is about - the birds!

questions.question: What is the predicate of this sentence: 'The birds sang in the morning.'?
questions.explanation: The predicate tells what the subject does.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the predicate tells what the subject did!

questions.question: Which sentence has a plural noun?
questions.correctAnswer: The children played in the park
distractors: The child played in the park
questions.explanation: Children is the plural form of child.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: children is more than one child!

questions.question: What is the plural of 'box'?
questions.explanation: Add -es to words ending in x, s, ch, or sh.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: box becomes boxes - add -es after x!

questions.question: What is the plural of 'baby'?
questions.explanation: Change y to i and add -es when a word ends in a consonant plus y.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: baby becomes babies - y turns to ies!

questions.question: What is the plural of 'child'?
questions.explanation: Child is irregular: its plural is children.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: child becomes children - an irregular plural!

questions.question: Which word is a verb in the past tense?
questions.explanation: Walked shows the action already happened.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: walked happened already - past tense!

questions.question: Which word is a verb in the future tense?
questions.explanation: Will walk shows the action will happen later.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: will walk is in the future!

questions.question: Which sentence uses the present tense correctly?
questions.correctAnswer: She reads a book every night
distractors: She readed a book every night
She will reads a book every night
She reading a book every night
questions.explanation: Reads matches the present tense for she.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: she reads - present tense, nice and simple!

questions.question: Which is the correct past tense of 'go'?
questions.explanation: Go is irregular: its past tense is went.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: go becomes went - irregular but true!

questions.question: Which is the correct past tense of 'eat'?
questions.explanation: Eat is irregular: its past tense is ate.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: eat becomes ate!

questions.question: Which sentence has correct subject-verb agreement?
questions.correctAnswer: The dogs run in the yard
distractors: The dogs runs in the yard
The dog run in the yard
The dogs running in the yard
questions.explanation: A plural subject (dogs) needs a plural verb (run).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: dogs run - plural subject, plural verb!

questions.question: Which sentence uses 'has' and 'have' correctly?
questions.explanation: She takes has; they takes have.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: she has - match the verb to the subject!

questions.question: Which word is an adjective in this sentence: 'The delicious cake was gone in minutes.'?
questions.explanation: Delicious describes the cake.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: delicious describes the cake!

questions.question: Which word is an adverb in this sentence: 'The turtle moved slowly.'?
questions.explanation: Slowly tells how the turtle moved.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: slowly tells how the turtle moved!

questions.question: Which sentence uses a comma correctly?
questions.correctAnswer: I bought apples, oranges, and bananas
distractors: I bought, apples oranges and bananas
I bought apples oranges, and bananas
I, bought apples oranges and bananas
questions.explanation: Commas separate items in a list.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: commas separate list items!

questions.question: Which sentence ends with the correct punctuation?
questions.explanation: A question ends with a question mark.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: questions end with a question mark!

questions.question: Which sentence uses quotation marks correctly?
distractors: Sara said I love this book.
Sara said, I love this book.
questions.explanation: Quotation marks go around the exact words someone says.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: quotation marks hug the exact spoken words!

questions.question: Which sentence uses an apostrophe correctly to show possession?
questions.explanation: An apostrophe plus s shows that something belongs to Maria.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Maria's bike - apostrophe s shows it is hers!

questions.question: Which is the correct contraction for 'do not'?
questions.explanation: Don't puts the apostrophe where the o is missing.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: do not becomes don't - the apostrophe takes the o's place!

questions.question: Which is the correct contraction for 'we will'?
questions.explanation: We'll drops the wi from will.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: we will becomes we'll!

questions.question: Which sentence needs capital letters in two places?
questions.correctAnswer: we went to the park on saturday
distractors: We went to the park on Saturday
we went to the park on Saturday
We went to the park on saturday
questions.explanation: Sentences and days of the week start with capitals.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Saturday and sentence starts get capitals!

questions.question: Which word should be capitalized in this sentence: 'My friend lives in texas'?
questions.explanation: State names are proper nouns and need capitals.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Texas is a proper noun - capital T!

questions.question: Which is the correct way to write the book title 'the lion, the witch and the wardrobe'?
questions.correctAnswer: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe
distractors: the lion, the witch and the wardrobe
The lion, The witch and The wardrobe
THE LION, THE WITCH AND THE WARDROBE
questions.explanation: Capitalize the important words in a title.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: book titles capitalize the important words!

questions.question: Where does a comma go in this sentence: 'After lunch we played outside'?
questions.explanation: A comma follows an introductory phrase like 'After lunch'.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a comma follows an opening phrase!

questions.question: Which sentence uses a comma correctly with a name?
questions.explanation: A comma sets off a name when speaking directly to someone.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: comma after a name you are speaking to!

questions.question: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
questions.correctAnswer: Wow, that was a great game!
distractors: Wow that was a great game!
Wow that was a great game.
Wow that was a great game?
questions.explanation: An exclamation shows strong feeling and needs an exclamation mark.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: wow deserves an exclamation mark!

questions.question: Which of these is a complete sentence?
questions.explanation: A complete sentence has a subject and a verb.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a sentence needs a subject and a verb!

questions.question: Which of these is a sentence fragment?
distractors: The dog ran through the park
questions.explanation: Running through the park has no subject, so it is a fragment.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a fragment is missing a subject or a verb!

questions.question: Which sentence is a run-on sentence?
questions.correctAnswer: I love soccer it is my favorite sport
distractors: I love soccer. It is my favorite sport.
I love soccer, and it is my favorite sport.
questions.explanation: A run-on joins two sentences without punctuation.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: two sentences stuck together is a run-on!

questions.question: How do you fix the run-on 'I was tired I went to bed'?
questions.correctAnswer: I was tired, so I went to bed
distractors: I was tired I went to bed.
I was tired, I went to bed
I was tired went to bed
questions.explanation: Join the sentences with a comma and a conjunction, or split them.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: add so and a comma to fix the run-on!

questions.question: Which sentence uses a period correctly with an abbreviation?
questions.correctAnswer: Dr. Smith will see you now.
distractors: Dr Smith will see you now.
Dr. Smith will see you now
Dr Smith will see you now
questions.explanation: Abbreviations like Dr. need a period, and the sentence ends with a period too.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Dr. needs its dot - and so does the sentence!

questions.question: Which sentence uses a colon correctly?
questions.correctAnswer: Bring these items: a pencil, a notebook, and an eraser
distractors: Bring these items a pencil, a notebook, and an eraser:
questions.explanation: A colon introduces a list after a complete sentence.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a colon says here comes a list!

questions.question: Which word needs an apostrophe in this sentence: 'The dog bone is under the table'?
questions.explanation: The bone belongs to one dog, so it is dog's.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: one dog's bone - apostrophe s!

questions.question: Which is correct: 'its' or 'it's' in this sentence: '___ raining outside'?
questions.explanation: It's is short for it is. Its shows possession.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: it is raining - so it's with an apostrophe!

questions.question: What does the prefix 'un-' mean?
questions.explanation: Un- means not, as in unhappy.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: un- means not!

questions.question: What does the prefix 're-' mean?
questions.explanation: Re- means again, as in redo.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: re- means again!

questions.question: What does the prefix 'pre-' mean?
questions.explanation: Pre- means before, as in preview.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: pre- means before!

questions.question: What does the prefix 'dis-' mean?
questions.explanation: Dis- means not or opposite, as in disagree.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: dis- flips the meaning to the opposite!

questions.question: What does the prefix 'mis-' mean?
questions.explanation: Mis- means wrongly, as in misunderstand.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: mis- means wrongly - misunderstand!

questions.question: What does the suffix '-ful' mean?
questions.explanation: -Ful means full of, as in careful.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: -ful means full of!

questions.question: What does the suffix '-less' mean?
questions.explanation: -Less means without, as in fearless.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: -less means without!

questions.question: What does the suffix '-er' often mean?
questions.explanation: -Er can mean one who does it, as in teacher.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: -er is the doer - a teacher teaches!

questions.question: What does the suffix '-ness' mean?
questions.correctAnswer: A state or quality of being
questions.explanation: -Ness turns an adjective into a noun, as in happiness.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: -ness names a quality - happiness!

questions.question: What does the root 'port' mean?
questions.explanation: Port means carry, as in transport and portable.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: port means carry - transport carries things!

questions.question: What does the root 'scrib' or 'script' mean?
questions.explanation: Scrib means write, as in describe and script.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: scrib means write - describe!

questions.question: What does the root 'aud' mean?
questions.explanation: Aud means hear, as in audience and audio.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: aud means hear - audience listens!

questions.question: What does the root 'vis' or 'vid' mean?
questions.explanation: Vis means see, as in visible and video.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: vis means see - visible!

questions.question: What does the word 'transport' mean, using the root 'port'?
questions.explanation: Trans- means across and port means carry, so transport is carry across.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: trans plus port equals carry across!

questions.question: What does the word 'preview' mean, using the prefix 'pre-'?
questions.explanation: Pre- means before and view means see, so preview is see before.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: pre plus view equals see before!

questions.question: What does the word 'fearless' mean?
questions.explanation: -Less means without, so fearless means without fear.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: fearless means without fear!

questions.question: What does the word 'helpful' mean?
questions.explanation: -Ful means full of, so helpful means full of help.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: helpful means full of help!

questions.question: What does the word 'misunderstand' mean?
questions.explanation: Mis- means wrongly, so misunderstand is understand wrongly.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: misunderstand means get it wrong!

questions.question: What is the root word in 'unhappiness'?
questions.explanation: Remove the prefix un- and the suffix -ness to find happy.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: strip un- and -ness and happy is left!

questions.question: What is the root word in 'disagreement'?
questions.explanation: Remove dis- and -ment to find agree.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: strip dis- and -ment and agree is left!

questions.question: Which word is a synonym for 'brave'?
questions.explanation: Courageous means brave.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: brave and courageous are twins!

questions.question: Which word is an antonym for 'ancient'?
questions.explanation: Ancient means very old; modern is its opposite.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: ancient and modern are opposites!

questions.question: Which word is a synonym for 'enormous'?
questions.explanation: Enormous and huge both mean very large.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: enormous and huge are twins!

questions.question: Which word is an antonym for 'generous'?
questions.explanation: Generous means giving freely; stingy is the opposite.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: generous gives, stingy keeps!

questions.question: Which word is a synonym for 'rapid'?
questions.explanation: Rapid and swift both mean very fast.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: rapid and swift are twins!

questions.question: Which word is an antonym for 'victory'?
questions.explanation: Victory means winning; defeat is losing.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: victory and defeat are opposites!

questions.question: Which word is a synonym for 'fragile'?
questions.explanation: Fragile and delicate both mean easily broken.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: fragile and delicate are twins!

questions.question: Which word is an antonym for 'honest'?
questions.explanation: Honest means truthful; dishonest is the opposite.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: honest and dishonest are opposites!

questions.question: Which word is a synonym for 'furious'?
questions.explanation: Furious and enraged both mean very angry.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: furious and enraged are twins!

questions.question: Which word is an antonym for 'scarce'?
questions.explanation: Scarce means hard to find; plentiful means there is lots.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: scarce and plentiful are opposites!

questions.question: Which sentence uses 'their' correctly?
distractors: Their is a cat on the roof
questions.explanation: Their shows possession: the dog belongs to them.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: their shows ownership - their dog!

questions.question: Which sentence uses 'there' correctly?
questions.correctAnswer: The book is over there on the shelf
questions.explanation: There points to a place.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: there points to a place - over there!

questions.question: Which sentence uses 'they're' correctly?
questions.correctAnswer: They're going to the park today
questions.explanation: They're is short for they are.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: they're means they are!

questions.question: Which sentence uses 'your' correctly?
questions.correctAnswer: Your shoes are by the door
questions.explanation: Your shows possession: the shoes belong to you.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: your shows ownership - your shoes!

questions.question: Which sentence uses 'you're' correctly?
questions.correctAnswer: You're going to love this book
distractors: You're shoes are by the door
Youre going to love this book
questions.explanation: You're is short for you are.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: you're means you are!

questions.question: Which sentence uses 'to', 'too', and 'two' correctly?
questions.correctAnswer: I have two apples, and I want to eat them too
distractors: I have to apples, and I want too eat them two
I have too apples, and I want two eat them to
I have two apples, and I want too eat them to
questions.explanation: Two is the number, to shows direction or purpose, too means also.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: two is the number, to is the direction, too means also!

questions.question: Which sentence uses 'its' correctly?
questions.explanation: Its shows possession with no apostrophe.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: its tail - no apostrophe for possession!

questions.question: Which sentence uses 'it's' correctly?
questions.explanation: It's is short for it is.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: it's raining means it is raining!

questions.question: Which word is the correct homophone: 'I can ___ the music from here'?
questions.explanation: Hear means to listen with your ears.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: hear with your ears!

questions.question: Which word completes the sentence: 'The ___ of the story was brave'?
questions.explanation: Hero is the main character, not hear (listen).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the hero is the brave main character!

questions.question: What does the idiom 'raining cats and dogs' mean?
distractors: Animals are falling from the sky
questions.explanation: Idioms mean something different from their literal words.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: raining cats and dogs means a heavy downpour!

questions.question: What does the idiom 'a piece of cake' mean?
questions.explanation: A piece of cake means an easy job.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a piece of cake means super easy!

questions.question: What does the idiom 'hit the books' mean?
questions.explanation: Hit the books means to begin studying hard.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: hit the books means start studying!

questions.question: What does the idiom 'under the weather' mean?
questions.explanation: Under the weather means feeling ill.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: under the weather means feeling sick!

questions.question: What does the idiom 'costs an arm and a leg' mean?
questions.explanation: Costs an arm and a leg means a very high price.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: costs an arm and a leg means super pricey!

questions.question: Which sentence uses a metaphor?
questions.explanation: A metaphor says one thing IS another without like or as.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: time is a thief - a metaphor!

questions.question: Which sentence uses hyperbole, or exaggeration?
questions.correctAnswer: I have a million things to do today
distractors: I have three things to do today
questions.explanation: Hyperbole is a huge exaggeration for effect.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a million things is exaggeration - hyperbole!

questions.question: Which sentence is a question?
distractors: My backpack is on the chair.
questions.explanation: A question asks something and ends with a question mark.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: questions ask and end with a question mark!

questions.question: Which sentence is a command?
questions.explanation: A command tells someone to do something.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a command tells you what to do!

questions.question: Which sentence is an exclamation?
questions.explanation: An exclamation shows strong feeling and ends with an exclamation mark.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: exclamations show big feelings!

questions.question: Which sentence is a statement?
questions.correctAnswer: The library opens at nine o'clock.
distractors: Does the library open at nine?
questions.explanation: A statement tells a fact and ends with a period.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a statement tells a fact!

questions.question: Which sentence is a compound sentence?
questions.correctAnswer: I wanted to swim, but the pool was closed
questions.explanation: A compound sentence joins two complete sentences with a conjunction.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: two sentences joined with but - compound!

questions.question: Which sentence is a complex sentence?
questions.correctAnswer: Because it was raining, we stayed inside
distractors: We stayed inside and played games.
questions.explanation: A complex sentence has a dependent clause (because it was raining) plus a main sentence.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: because it was raining - a dependent clause makes it complex!

questions.question: Which word is a conjunction that joins two sentences?
questions.explanation: And, but, and or join words and sentences.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: and joins things together!

questions.question: What is the subject of this sentence: 'After the game, the tired players walked home.'?
questions.explanation: The subject is who the sentence is about: the players.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the players are who the sentence is about!
